title: More on Then She Fell / Third Rail: @Joe Weinberg  #immersive #theatre
transcript: We got some immersive theatre news this week that's exciting, but also funny. Maybe only to me, though. It was announced that the immersive theatre company Punchdrunk, best known for sleep no more, is going to do a co-production with the National Theatre in London. Now, this isn't the first collaboration between these two major British theatre companies, but it's the first one in quite a while. And this one does appear to be different. unlike their other collaborations, It sounds, from the way this is worded, like this immersive theater piece is going to be performed in or around the National Theater's main building. And for those who don't know, the National Theater at South Bank is a pretty massive building, so this could look like a lot of different things. But the reason this is funny to me is that there already was an immersive theater show called Ghost Light that used the lobby and backstage areas of a real life theater as their immersive promenade playground. It was back in 2017, performed in and around the Clair Tow Theater at Lincoln Center. And it was created by the immersive company Third Rail Projects. Third Rail Projects is kind of a competitor with Punchdrunk, probably not in a contentious way. And no tea, no shade. I love Third Rail projects. I did a whole video about the evolution of their style and their work, which I'll link in the caption. But as much as they do have their Own style. I think there's always been a sense, especially at the beginning, that Third Rail Projects was kind of following in the wake of PunchDrunk. And that's why it's funny to me that Punchdrunk might be doing something that Third Rail Projects kind of already did, especially with the same title.
